passage:
Monday: After their fight about his job move, Nitin went silent. Jahnavi followed him from the kitchen to the balcony. "Talk to me! Why do you always do this?" He put on his headphones and went for a walk. She sent nine messages. No reply till midnight.
Thursday: At the next disagreement, she tried something different. "I can see you're shutting down. I need us to finish this. Can we pick it up on Sunday evening, after dinner?" He blinked, then nodded.
Sunday: At eight he came to the table, a bit stiff, and talked for twenty minutes. When he began drifting off again, Jahnavi said calmly, "It's okay to pause. It's not okay to vanish for days. That's my limit." He sat back down.

qa.q: How many messages did Jahnavi send on Monday?
qa.a: She sent nine messages.

qa.q: What was Jahnavi feeling on Monday when she followed Nitin, and what shows it?
qa.a: She felt shut out and desperate; she followed him from room to room and asked why he always does this.

qa.q: What changed on Thursday, and why did it work better?
qa.a: She calmly named his shutting down and asked to continue at a set time, which gave him space without dropping her need.

qa.q: How might Nitin experience a calm request compared with being chased?
qa.a: Being chased probably made him feel cornered, so he left; a calm, timed request felt manageable, so he came back.

grounding: Over a week, a woman whose partner goes quiet in conflict moves from chasing him to calm, direct requests and a clear personal limit.

passage: Come, sit with your old Sarita ammachi. When I married your grandfather Thomas, I was twenty-five and he was a closed box. Any quarrel, he would walk out to the church compound and sit there for hours. I used to run after him, crying, pulling his sleeve, and he only went further, to the fish market, anywhere. One evening my own mother said, "You are chasing a cat. Sit still and tell him plainly." So the next time, I said, "Thomas, when you leave in the middle, I feel alone. Come back in one hour and we'll finish." Then I made my tea and did not follow. He came back in forty minutes. It took years, but he learned to stay. And I learned to stop running.

qa.q: Where would Thomas go after a quarrel?
qa.a: He would walk out to the church compound and sit there for hours.

qa.q: What did Sarita feel when Thomas left in the middle of a quarrel?
qa.a: She felt alone and upset, which is why she used to run after him crying.

qa.q: What was the turning point in how Sarita handled quarrels?
qa.a: She told Thomas plainly how she felt, asked him to come back in one hour and stopped following him.

qa.q: How might Thomas have felt when Sarita stopped chasing him?
qa.a: He probably felt less cornered, which made it easier to return on his own; he came back in forty minutes.

grounding: A grandmother recalls feeling shut out by a husband who left during quarrels, and how calm, plain requests worked better than chasing.

passage: For the first year I chased. Whenever my wife, Payal, went silent in a fight, I followed her from room to room: "What's wrong? Talk to me!" louder each time. She'd go to the balcony, then put her headphones on, then leave for a walk. I'm Rafiq, and I felt invisible in my own flat. One night a friend asked, "Does chasing ever work?" It never had. So I tried something else. When she went quiet about my mother's visit, I said once, calmly, "I need us to decide by Sunday. Can we talk after dinner?" Then I made tea. She came into the kitchen at nine. I also told her I won't keep having fights with a closed door. That limit is mine to keep.

qa.q: Where did Payal go first when Rafiq followed her?
qa.a: To the balcony.

qa.q: How did Rafiq feel during the year of chasing?
qa.a: Rafiq felt invisible and shut out, and grew louder as Payal withdrew further.

qa.q: What changed, and why did it work better?
qa.a: Rafiq made one calm, direct request with a time and then gave space, which let Payal come back on her own.

qa.q: What might it be like for Payal when Rafiq follows her from room to room?
qa.a: Payal likely feels cornered, so she retreats further to the balcony, headphones and walks.

grounding: Shows a partner who feels shut out, learns that chasing drives the other away, and uses a calm request and a personal limit.

passage: Session note, couple's session two. Vidya did most of the talking again. When she described last week's argument about Jagdish's late nights at the lab, he looked at the floor and said, "It's not a big deal." I watched her hands clench and her voice rise; she leaned forward, repeating herself. He leaned further back. I paused them and asked Vidya to say, slowly, one sentence about what she needed. She said, "When you go quiet, I feel alone. I need ten minutes of talk each night, even if it's short." Jagdish looked up for the first time. I noted her relief. Next step: both will try the ten minutes this week, and I will see Jagdish alone once to hear his side.

qa.q: What did Jagdish say about the argument?
qa.a: "It's not a big deal."

qa.q: What was Vidya feeling as she repeated herself?
qa.a: She felt alone and dismissed, with clenched hands and a rising voice.

qa.q: Why did the one slow sentence work better than repeating herself?
qa.a: A calm, specific request was easier for Jagdish to hear than pressure, so he looked up instead of leaning back.

qa.q: How might Jagdish experience Vidya leaning forward and repeating herself?
qa.a: He may feel pressured and retreat further, which is why he leaned back.

grounding: Illustrates a partner who feels shut out during conflict, and how a calm, direct request works better than chasing.

passage:
Thursday. Vandana did it again tonight. I said I felt hurt that she'd booked the trip without asking, and she said, "You're overthinking," and went to the balcony with her phone. Old me would have followed her out, pleaded, maybe cried, and she'd have gone even quieter. Tonight I didn't. I sat with my tea, heart thumping, and texted her from the sofa, ten feet away: "I'm not going to chase you. When you're ready, I want to talk about how we decide trips. I'll be up till eleven." At 10.20 she came in and sat at the other end of the sofa. We didn't solve it. But she stayed.
Sudha

qa.q: What time did Vandana come in?
How did Sudha feel when Vandana said "You're overthinking"?
qa.a: Sudha felt hurt and dismissed, heart thumping, but chose not to chase this time.

qa.q: What made Sudha's text a wise response?
qa.a: It stayed calm, named a clear request and a time, and set a limit on chasing.

qa.q: How might Vandana experience the text instead of being followed?
qa.a: Vandana may feel less cornered and freer to come back, which she did by sitting on the sofa.

grounding: Shows a partner who feels shut out and chooses a calm, direct request and personal limit over chasing.

passage:
Hrithik: you went silent again after the argument about your parents' visit
Hrithik: it's been two days
Jatin: I'm just busy
Hrithik: I've sent you five messages. I'm not going to send ten
Hrithik: here's what I need: when we disagree, I need you to say "I need a few hours" instead of disappearing
Jatin: you're making it a big deal
Hrithik: it is a big deal to me. I'll give you space till Sunday. If we can't talk by then, I'll go to my sister's for the weekend and we'll talk after
Jatin: ok
Jatin: ...sorry. I shut down when things get loud
Hrithik: I know. I'm not chasing. I'm asking. Sunday, 6 pm?
Jatin: Sunday 6

qa.q: How many messages had Hrithik already sent?
qa.a: Five messages.

qa.q: What was Hrithik feeling during Jatin's two days of silence?
qa.a: Hrithik felt shut out and hurt, but stayed calm, deciding not to send ten messages.

qa.q: Why is Hrithik's approach wiser than chasing?
qa.a: Hrithik makes a calm, direct request and sets a clear limit with a Sunday talk, instead of chasing, which usually makes Jatin retreat further.

qa.q: How might Jatin see the silence from the inside?
qa.a: Jatin says shutting down happens when things get loud, so the silence may feel like protection rather than a way of dismissing Hrithik.

grounding: Shows a partner shut out by silence after conflict choosing a calm, direct request and a personal limit instead of chasing.
